recent_commits.message: Fix ResearchBox file-link collapsing and Stata quoted-filename regex
recent_commits.body:
ResearchBox hrefs pointing at a specific file within a box (e.g. a dotted
box variant or a numeric file id under the box) were treated as separate
repos; they are now truncated to the box id so all such links collapse to
the one box before repo_check sees them.

The unquoted-filename capture regexes in code_file_refs() were matching
inside already-quoted Stata filenames that contain spaces, producing bogus
extra references; they now only run against lines without a quoted
filename.

Ported from the reproducibility_check branch (efedd30), which bundled these
with reproducibility_check()-specific changes that do not apply here since
that module isn't on dev yet.
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Report inaccessible OSF registration links instead of dropping them silently (#361)
recent_commits.body:
osf_type() already tells "not a registration" apart from "a registration link that cannot be read" (private, embargoed, withdrawn, or deleted), but prereg_check.R only ever used the former, so an inaccessible registration read identically to no registration being linked at all. Now tracked from both osf_type()'s "inaccessible" classification and a later fetch failure (osf_get_all_pages()'s osf_error attribute), and named in both summary_text and the full report.

Added a guard for the resulting zero-row edge case (every link inaccessible, no AsPredicted data) that would otherwise fall through to code assuming a paper_id column that is only added when prereg_info has rows.

Tests use testthat::with_mocked_bindings() rather than local_mocked_bindings(): the latter's deferred cleanup does not restore correctly through this project's custom test_that() wrapper in helper.R and leaks into whichever test runs next (same class of issue test-archive-osf.R's .osf_status_error test already flags for req_perform()).
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Remove FLoRA_update() mock test and its oversized fixture (#364)
recent_commits.body:
The "update" test only asserted file.exists(path) on the download result, never its content or size, so its mock fixture recorded the real 5.6MB flora.csv as a 37MB text file checked into the repo for a test that needed none of it. It was also gated behind skip_if_quick(), so it never ran in a normal test pass. Not worth reconstructing a smaller fixture for; removed the test and both its fixtures (download body + guid listing).

Also confirms the mode = "all" default-change audit from #364: FLoRA_update() (R/db-replications.R) was the only affected caller, already fixed in 431e0c5. No other caller in R/, inst/app/, or tests/ relies on the old implicit default.
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix inconsistent quoting in ethics_check.R @details phrasing (#360)
recent_commits.body: Pattern examples in the "Patterns are designed to capture" section used plain double quotes, which roxygen renders as literal quote-mark characters rather than a code span. Converted to backticks throughout the section for consistent rendering.
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Improve GROBID/BIBR isalive error handling (#363)
recent_commits.body: .grobid_isalive() and .bibr_isalive() discarded the real httr2 error and replaced it with a generic message, making transient failures hard to diagnose. Both now include conditionMessage(e) in the error, and retry on connection-level failure (not just HTTP transient responses) so a live server surviving a one-off blip doesn't fail the whole conversion.
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix power.R optional enum fields rejecting null on Groq (#365)
recent_commits.body: ellmer's ProviderOpenAICompatible adds "null" to a type_enum(required = FALSE) field's type but never adds null to its enum, so Groq's response-side validator rejects a genuinely null response even though its own request-side schema allows it. Adding NA to each optional enum's value vector matches power.json's null-inclusive enums and fixes the mismatch (confirmed live against Groq).
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

ResearchBox hrefs pointing at a specific file within a box were treated as

now only run against lines without a quoted filename. reproducibility_check()
gains a cache argument forwarded to data_check/code_check, and duplicate-file
reporting now shows each mirror's location instead of just its (identical)
basename.

recent_commits.message: Normalize line endings repo-wide with a single text=auto rule
recent_commits.body:
.gitattributes previously forced LF only under tests/testthat/fixtures/,
which also matched binary fixtures there (PDFs, a zip) and forced git to
treat them as text, and left every other CRLF-committed text file (e.g.
data-raw/demo/ground_truth/*.csv, tests/testthat/apis/**/*.html) subject to
each contributor's local core.autocrlf, causing line-ending-only diffs on
checkout.

Replace it with `* text=auto`: git decides text vs. binary from each file's
actual content (the same detection diff/file use), not its extension or
path, so a binary file with a misleading name (e.g. the zip archive stored
as tests/testthat/apis/.../osfstorage-546010.R-FILE) is still handled
correctly with no entry needed, and every genuine text file is stored and
checked out as LF regardless of the checkout platform.

Renormalizes the 23 tracked text files that were actually stored with CRLF
(verified byte-for-byte: only line-ending bytes changed, no content diff).

recent_commits.message: Fix remaining test warnings, including a cross-file llm_use() leak
recent_commits.body:
test-module-power.R's last test block set llm_use(TRUE) and never
reset it, leaking that global option into every test file that ran
afterward in the suite. test-module-repo_check.R and
test-repo-download.R were the two downstream files that triggered
real (unmocked) LLM network calls as a side effect, failing with
connection-refused and printing as warnings even though their actual
assertions still passed. Fixed with withr::defer(llm_use(FALSE)) --
plain on.exit() and withr::local_options() were both tried first and
confirmed, by direct testing, not to restore state correctly through
this project's custom test_that() wrapper in helper.R; withr::defer()
does. Applied the same fix to test-llm.R and test-utils.R, which had
the same unrestored llm_use(TRUE) pattern.

test-archive-zenodo.R and test-repo-download.R had intentional
fake-download-failure scenarios whose warnings were never wrapped in
expect_warning(), the same gap already fixed in
test-archive-dataverse.R -- applied consistently here too.

Full suite: 0 failures, 0 warnings, 4280 passed.

recent_commits.message: Fix R CMD check warnings/notes and cross-test pollution from dead module imports
recent_commits.body:
R CMD check fixes:
- .Rbuildignore: exclude .vscode, .comments, CLAUDE.md; delete stray
  duplicate to_err_is_human.xml at repo root (real copy lives in
  inst/demos/)
- Non-ASCII characters warning: escape functional Unicode (Greek
  statistical notation, math operators, box-drawing table borders, a
  field-separator character, an NBSP constant, a BOM string) as \uXXXX,
  substitute purely decorative comment punctuation with ASCII, across
  12 files
- Undeclared imports warning: add SnowballC, data.table, officer,
  pdftools, readxl, yaml to Suggests (already used via :: throughout)
- Rd cross-references / Rd usage-section warnings: two roxygen blocks
  had drifted onto the wrong function because a plain (non-roxygen)
  comment sat between the doc block and its real target
  (stat_results_long, data_read_head) -- moved each block to the
  correct function; removed one duplicate leftover block; stripped six
  dangling \link{} references to functions that only exist on unmerged
  branches
- R code NOTE: qualify two bare ave() calls as stats::ave(), fix an NSE
  binding in code_setwd(), port the missing .repro_split_args() helper
  r-output.R was calling (only defined on the reproducibility_check
  branch)
- Avoid the "assignments to the global environment" NOTE in
  .r_capture_runner() (a callr subprocess payload, not the user's
  session) by capturing globalenv() into a variable first, which
  R CMD check's static scan does not resolve

Test suite fix:
- Three modules (prereg_check.R, code_check.R, stat_effect_size.R)
  declared roxygen @import for packages (httr, jsonlite, tidyr) they
  never actually use. module_run() require()s every declared @import,
  so running those modules' tests attached httr/jsonlite to the search
  path ahead of metacheck, letting httr::verbose() and
  jsonlite::validate() shadow metacheck::verbose()/validate() for every
  test that ran afterward in the same session -- the reason two
  unrelated test files only failed in full-suite runs, never in
  isolation. Removed the three dead @import lines (a full sweep confirms
  no other module has an unused import).

recent_commits.message: Fix two unrelated OSF test bugs surfaced by the httr2 upgrade
recent_commits.body:
test-archive-osf_file_download.R's hand-mocked req_perform() lacked
the mock parameter that httr2 1.3.0's req_perform_sequential() now
passes through, causing "unused argument (mock = mock)". Its mock_id
"abcde" is also 5 characters, the same shape as a real OSF user GUID,
so .osf_expand_user_ids() (added recently to support whole-project
downloads) treated it as a possible user and called the live,
unmocked osf_type() API to check. Both fixed: the mock signature
accepts mock now, and osf_type is mocked to report "nodes".

test-import-read.R's recursive-read test hardcoded the expected paper
order as a fixed positional pattern, which happened to match
read()'s actual behaviour (list.files(recursive = TRUE), alphabetical
by path) only by coincidence with the old corpus's specific paper
IDs. Rewritten to derive the expectation the same way read() does,
so it verifies the real contract instead of one corpus's ID strings.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Load psychsci from scienceverse/papers instead of bundling it
recent_commits.body:
The psychsci example corpus (250 Psychological Science open-access
papers) was a 4.4 MB .rda shipped with the package purely for
documentation examples, counting against CRAN's package size limit.
It is now fetched via papers_load("psychsci", cache = TRUE), the same
mechanism already used for every other corpus on scienceverse/papers
(published as a new "psychsci" release there, containing the original
data). Examples across paper.R, module.R, text_expand.R, and every
archive-*.R file are updated to load it explicitly and wrapped in
\dontrun{}, matching papers_load()'s own documented example.

data-raw/psychsci/ (the multi-version grobid/bibr extraction pipeline
that built the old .rda, repeatedly re-committed across development)
is removed entirely: the corpus it produced no longer lives in this
repository.
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Stop tracking pkgdown docs/ and unused RegCheck assets
recent_commits.body:
docs/ is fully generated by pkgdown and already has a CI workflow
(.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml) that can deploy it to gh-pages, so it
no longer needs to be committed alongside source. inst/templates/_report.html

_new_commits.body:

_new_commits.message: Report inaccessible OSF registration links instead of dropping them silently (#361)
_new_commits.body:
osf_type() already tells "not a registration" apart from "a registration link that cannot be read" (private, embargoed, withdrawn, or deleted), but prereg_check.R only ever used the former, so an inaccessible registration read identically to no registration being linked at all. Now tracked from both osf_type()'s "inaccessible" classification and a later fetch failure (osf_get_all_pages()'s osf_error attribute), and named in both summary_text and the full report.

Added a guard for the resulting zero-row edge case (every link inaccessible, no AsPredicted data) that would otherwise fall through to code assuming a paper_id column that is only added when prereg_info has rows.

Tests use testthat::with_mocked_bindings() rather than local_mocked_bindings(): the latter's deferred cleanup does not restore correctly through this project's custom test_that() wrapper in helper.R and leaks into whichever test runs next (same class of issue test-archive-osf.R's .osf_status_error test already flags for req_perform()).
_new_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

_new_commits.message: Remove FLoRA_update() mock test and its oversized fixture (#364)
_new_commits.body:
The "update" test only asserted file.exists(path) on the download result, never its content or size, so its mock fixture recorded the real 5.6MB flora.csv as a 37MB text file checked into the repo for a test that needed none of it. It was also gated behind skip_if_quick(), so it never ran in a normal test pass. Not worth reconstructing a smaller fixture for; removed the test and both its fixtures (download body + guid listing).

Also confirms the mode = "all" default-change audit from #364: FLoRA_update() (R/db-replications.R) was the only affected caller, already fixed in 431e0c5. No other caller in R/, inst/app/, or tests/ relies on the old implicit default.
_new_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

_new_commits.message: Fix inconsistent quoting in ethics_check.R @details phrasing (#360)
_new_commits.body: Pattern examples in the "Patterns are designed to capture" section used plain double quotes, which roxygen renders as literal quote-mark characters rather than a code span. Converted to backticks throughout the section for consistent rendering.
_new_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

_new_commits.message: Improve GROBID/BIBR isalive error handling (#363)
_new_commits.body: .grobid_isalive() and .bibr_isalive() discarded the real httr2 error and replaced it with a generic message, making transient failures hard to diagnose. Both now include conditionMessage(e) in the error, and retry on connection-level failure (not just HTTP transient responses) so a live server surviving a one-off blip doesn't fail the whole conversion.
_new_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

_new_commits.message: Fix power.R optional enum fields rejecting null on Groq (#365)
_new_commits.body: ellmer's ProviderOpenAICompatible adds "null" to a type_enum(required = FALSE) field's type but never adds null to its enum, so Groq's response-side validator rejects a genuinely null response even though its own request-side schema allows it. Adding NA to each optional enum's value vector matches power.json's null-inclusive enums and fixes the mismatch (confirmed live against Groq).
_new_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix `grim_plot()` dropping data, and drop its dead version branch
recent_commits.body:
The axis bounds were scale limits, which discard a tile as soon as one of
its edges falls outside. A mean of 5.00 has a fractional portion of exactly 0,
so its tile reached half its height below the axis and was dropped whole --
`pigs1` contains such a value, so the plot in the package's own examples had
been showing eleven of its twelve value sets. They are coordinate limits now,
which clip instead of discarding.

Negative means are plotted at the fractional portion of their absolute value,
so -2.51 is drawn at 0.51, in the same place as 2.51. GRIM's granularity is
symmetric around zero. Previously such a value fell outside the axis and was
dropped without a word. The new `Negative means` section explains the one
thing the sign still affects: for a one-directional `rounding` method the
raster behind a negative value is the mirrored method's. The tile's color is
unaffected, coming from the `consistency` column.

The blanket `suppressWarnings()` around the final `print()` is gone; it had
hidden both of the above. `show_raster = FALSE` works again -- the plot object
was only created inside the branch that draws the raster, so the documented
argument failed with "object 'p' not found". A zero-row `data` is now an
explained error instead of R's "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed".

The data is drawn by one `geom_tile()` call using `linewidth`. There were two,
chosen at run time on `utils::packageVersion("ggplot2") >= "3.4"`; DESCRIPTION
has required ggplot2 (>= 3.4.0) ever since, so the `size` branch was
unreachable and its deprecation warning was being suppressed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Fix DEBIT's false alarm at a reported mean of 0.50
recent_commits.body:
`debit_scalar()` reconstructed the SD at the two bounds of the mean's
rounding interval and concluded that every SD in between was reachable. That is
an intermediate-value argument and it needs monotonicity, which
`sd_binary_mean_n()` does not have: it is a downward parabola peaking at a mean
of 0.5. An interval containing 0.5 reaches SDs above both endpoints, and for a
mean of exactly 0.50 the interval is symmetric around the peak, so both
endpoints give the same SD and the attainable band collapsed to a point.
`debit(x = 0.50, sd = 0.503, n = 100, digits_x = 2, digits_sd = 3)` was FALSE
for 50 ones and 50 zeros. The peak is now evaluated too. The error only ever
turned TRUE into FALSE, so nothing that used to pass now fails.

Also rejects a `formula` other than "mean_n" with the package's own error. The
others need a group size DEBIT is not given, so they reached
`reconstruct_sd()` and failed with R's "argument \"group_0\" is missing",
about an argument the user never saw.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Resolve sequence-mapper dispersion limits per variable
recent_commits.body:
`out_min = "auto"` meant one decimal unit above zero for every dispersed
variable, though it was written for `n`. For a negative reported mean it
removed the whole lower half of the sequence, and 0 -- a legal mean, SD, and
proportion -- was out of reach everywhere. `function_map_seq()` gains
`.var_bounds`, and "auto" now resolves through it per variable: `n` keeps a
floor of 1 whether declared or not, GRIMMER's `sd` gets 0, DEBIT's `x` and
`sd` get [0, 1], and a mean is unbounded. `.out_max` defaults to "auto" for
the same reason. This also fixes `debit_map_seq()` failing outright whenever a
reported value sat close enough to 0 or 1 for the dispersion to cross it.

`reverse_map_seq()` no longer infers the reported value from the shape of the
sequence -- the midpoint of its gap, or its median if it had none. That is only
valid for a complete sequence: once a limit had truncated one side, the gap
disappeared and the median branch returned a plausible wrong number, so
`audit_seq()` on a reported mean of -2.51 gave -2.48 and the opposite verdict.
The value now comes from the `diff_var` column, which records how many steps
each row sits from it. `index_case_interpolate()` is replaced by
`index_case_from_diff()`, which errors rather than guessing when a group's
rows disagree.

The "no inconsistent cases" warning now always names `include_consistent`. It
named the R argument only when `interactive()` was TRUE and otherwise told the
user to untick a checkbox in the Shiny app -- so scripts, R Markdown, and test
runs got the checkbox message.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Drop zero steps in `seq_disperse()`'s `dispersion`
recent_commits.body:
A value in `dispersion` is a number of steps taken both up and down from
`from`, so a step of 0 is `from` itself, once in each direction. Whether
`from` belongs in its own sequence is what `include_reported` decides, so a
zero step added it two more times: `seq_disperse(4.02, dispersion = 0)` was
three copies of "4.02", and `grim_map_seq(dispersion = c(0, 1, 2))` returned
the reported case twice, which `audit_seq()` counted twice.

Also documents what `out_min = "auto"` suits and what to pass instead. It
resolves to one decimal unit above zero, which is right for a count and wrong
for anything that can reach zero or go negative.

recent_commits.message: release: v2.4.137 — a fix in the COMPARISON KEY is not a fix in the SHIPPED string
recent_commits.body:
v1.9.57 diagnosed that one stray U+0008 BACKSPACE made a Frontiers running
header unequal to its layout-channel twin, and fixed it inside `_key()` — F0's
comparison key. The character stayed in the emitted text, where a completely
unrelated rule landed on it one day later:
`_prior_paragraph_is_sentence_terminated` walks back over whitespace and
requires what it finds to be in ".!?/". On 10.3389/fvets.2025.1645266 the walk
landed on the BACKSPACE, discarded the `1 Introduction:` heading, and greedy
span-fill handed the preceding KEYWORDS span 69,849 characters — the whole
article. Found by an external benchmark, not by us.

* C0 `_strip_furniture_controls` (NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.58), run before F0
  so the comparison key and the output are ONE rule. One character wide and
  measured: all 33 corpus U+0008 sites are '.'+BS+newline, none are overstrike.
  U+0002/03/04/07 are corrupted CONTENT glyphs (Schri<02>macher =
  "Schrittmacher") and are COUNTED, not stripped, in the new
  `NormalizationReport.residual_control_chars`.
* The heading guard skips page breaks and control characters, and a canonical
  heading carrying BOTH a line-initial section number AND a colon no longer
  needs a terminated prior paragraph (SECTIONING_VERSION 1.2.5). Both halves
  are required: `2 Literature search` on the same paper resolves canonically to
  `references`, so a number-only escape would open back-matter mid-article.
  Measured blast radius: 3 of 39 guard rejections were furniture; the escape
  fires exactly once in 30 papers.

recent_commits.message: fix(normalize): a page NUMBER is furniture, a page BOUNDARY is structure
recent_commits.body:
`_normalize_text` stripped standalone page numbers with

    re.sub(r"^\s*\d{1,3}\s*$", "", t, flags=re.MULTILINE)

and under MULTILINE the whitespace class matches THE FORM FEED, so the rule could
consume the page boundary standing beside the number it was deleting. It had been
wrong since it was written, and a running footer sitting between the two held it
latent. The moment anything stripped that footer, every form feed in the document
went with it -- and with them the `\n\f\f\n` marker that separates the footnote
appendix, folding it back into the body where a consumer reads it as running text.

Two papers in the render baseline were ALREADY in that state at HEAD: they report
15 and 18 footnotes through `report.footnote_texts` while the returned string
carries no appendix at all. Nothing had ever noticed, because nothing compared
the two.

MEASURED, 26-paper baseline vs a `git worktree` of HEAD, extracted in separate
interpreters and diffed per field:

    lines removed / added (full text)     0 / 0
    papers gaining page breaks           16   (+1 to +17 each)
    footnote appendices RESTORED          2   (0 -> 1,288 and 0 -> 2,165 bytes)
    papers made worse on any metric        0

The rule is now `_strip_standalone_page_numbers()` -- a named function, so its
test pins THE SHIPPED RULE rather than a retyped copy of the pattern. The form
feed is CAPTURED and put back, not merely excluded from the class: a page number
is often the first thing on a new page, so the line itself begins with the break,
and excluding it stopped those lines matching at all ('496'..'502' reappeared in
the body of 10.1016/j.jesp.2009.12.010). `_drop()` in F0's strip loop keeps the
same promise from the other side -- the segment split attaches a separator to the
line BEFORE it, so deleting a running footer deleted its page break too.

All three guards mutation-verified: the original defect fails two tests, the
`[ \t]` half-fix fails one, neutering `_drop()` fails one. That last became a
real test only after the fixture was corrected -- it first put the furniture at
the TOP of each page, so its separator was a newline, `_drop()` was never
reached, and the test passed with the guard removed.

`_key` is hoisted to module level and strips non-whitespace control characters
(pdftotext emits a running header as FF + text + BACKSPACE). It is a correctness
fix to a key BOTH channels use; it changes no measured output today and its test
says so plainly rather than implying a capability.

ALSO: tools/diag/fused_cell_geometry_scan.py, the FUSED-GRID detector register
G6h was blocked on until v2.4.135 gave every Camelot cell a verified rectangle.
Validated on the census's own known positives before any count was quoted --
'104594' fires at 15.15 em (136.4 pt) between '4' and '5', '4.603.804.80' at
12.22 em. 80 fused cells, 1.13% of 7,065 measured, against the text-only
census's 34 (0.29%). Threshold measured, not chosen: 71,733 intra-cell gaps give
p50=0.00 p90=0.00 p99=0.33 em, so 0.75 sits in an empty band. It REFUSES any cell
whose recovered glyphs are not its own text (3,139 of 10,215) rather than folding
them into the denominator -- the first draft did not, and reported 17.3 em
"fusions" that were column gutters between two cells.

TWO REVERTS, both recorded because the reasoning is worth more than the code:

W0g/W0b/W0d are untouched here, but W0g is now DECIDED for deletion in its own
release: re-measured at 12 sites in 4 of 250 papers where the record said 4, and
at least 7 rewrite a quantity that is non-negative by definition. Confirmed on
the rasterized page -- 10.1525/collabra.118835 p7 prints
`hedges' g = -.17, SE = 0.11, ...` and W0g emits `SE = -0.11`.

repetition may bless it), L-054 ("no statistical content removed" is not "no

real coordinates for each one. Reading `ct.cells[r][c]` is one line; it took two
releases because EVERY way of getting it wrong produces WRONG coordinates rather
than empty ones, and a wrong bbox is worse than none - it answers, plausibly, and
the answer is off by a page. Register G4 deferred the work until the guard could
be built first. Building the guard found TWO MORE TRAPS G4 never listed, both
live on real papers:

  T5  Camelot silently ROTATES a page whose text is sideways and reports
      coordinates in that frame. 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.39337 p8:
      rotation=anticlockwise, pdf_size=(792,612), table bbox reaching x=730.7 -
      off-page in pdfplumber's 612-wide frame - while pdfplumber reports
      rotation=0. Also 10.1017/s0007123424000024 p6 (clockwise), whose converted
      boxes come out with a NEGATIVE top. 2 of 8 papers probed.
  T6  `_augment_lattice_with_stream_rows` pd.concat's stream rows onto `ct.df`
      and never touches `ct.cells`. 10.1038/s41598-023-50423-7 ships df=61x4
      against cells=20x4; zipping by index would give 41 rows of published data
      another row's rectangle.

THE GUARD. Each rectangle is converted to pdfplumber space, `chars_in_bbox` is
asked what stands there, and the result scored by character-multiset CONTAINMENT.
Exact equality is the wrong predicate and the probe said so before the code was
written: Camelot assigns a whole text object to ONE grid cell even when its
glyphs spill past that cell's column edges. Measured - per cell 86.3% score >=
0.95 under the correct transform against 2.1%/1.5%/1.5% under T1/T2/T3; per TABLE

trap. Gate 0.60, in a real gap: the lowest ACCEPTED table scores 0.70, the two
rejected 0.55 and 0.53. All-or-nothing per table.

Verification is SAMPLED (40 cells, fixed stride - never random); the geometry is
not. `chars_in_bbox` is O(chars-on-page), so full verification costs 78.9
ms/table and grows with the grid, on the service's per-request path; the cap
makes it 40.0 ms/table independent of size and changed NO verdict across 200
tables.

The three row-trims each gained an index-returning `_keep_after_*` sibling and
became one-liners over it - one implementation, two views, so the raw-row mapping
cannot drift from the trim. Behaviour verified identical to the originals over
6,002 generated matrices.

`Table["cell_geometry"]` is new, on EVERY table from EVERY path: "verified:<f>"
or the named refusal. An earlier draft set it only on the Camelot path and the
census caught 11.6% of tables reporting nothing - which both hid the state and
UNDERSTATED what we ship, since the whitespace path's boxes are built from
pdfplumber words and are real by construction.

  verified, 10.1% no_cells, 2.9% roundtrip_failed, 2.9% grid_shape_mismatch,

* full suite: 2840 passed, 27 skipped, 5 xfailed, 0 failed (1:03:51). 2872

`scripts/verify_corpus.py` now gets everything from article-finder: the expected
paper set, every PDF, and every baseline. No directory glob, no
`../PDFextractor/test-pdfs` coupling, no `DOCPLUCK_SPIKE_BASELINE_DIR`, no
`docs/superpowers/` default path. Papers are addressed by canonical key
(`--paper 10.1177/19485506211056761`).

**The coverage defect.** The gate derived its corpus from `glob("*.md")` and
printed `N / N` where N was whatever it found -- so a half-present corpus
reported a clean pass and a vanished one reported nothing at all. A denominator
computed from the numerator can only ever say 100%. It now comes from
`papers-with-view`, and three states are kept distinct:

  nothing resolvable        SKIP,    exit 0   (this machine has no corpus)
  some but not all          PARTIAL, exit 1   (the silent-shrink bug)
  all resolved              PASS/WARN/FAIL

New `PDF_DRIFT` status: the repository's copy of a paper is not the
manifestation the baseline was built from. Rendering one and comparing it to a
baseline built from the other measures nothing, and would print the difference
as a docpluck regression -- publisher PDF, arXiv preprint and PMC author
manuscript share a DOI but not bytes. It surfaced three such papers immediately.

**Re-baselined onto the repository's own copies**, which removes PDF_DRIFT by
construction: the artifact and the input the gate re-renders are now the same
bytes. Done only after all 26 papers verified against the 2026-05-10 prototype
baseline with ZERO failures (23 in the corpus run, 3 individually once their
drift was diagnosed) -- a baseline captured from unverified output bakes in
whatever was wrong at capture time. The prototype set stays registered as

`--baseline-view`.

paper report as simply absent:

- `10.1093/sf/soaf022` keys as `10.1093__sf__soaf022`; replacing only the FIRST
  `__` produced a DOI matching nothing. Every `__` is an encoded `/`.
- Two PDFs were ingested under a non-normalized mixed-case DOI, so the
  lower-cased gold key could never find them. Fixed in `ingest-local-pdf.py`
  (it now uses `_lib.normalize_doi` rather than a hand-rolled prefix strip), and
  5 pre-existing unreachable index keys were normalized or removed.
- `verified == 0` returned exit 0 as a clean SKIP even when every paper had
  ERRORed or drifted -- a green run reported because everything failed. It now
  skips only when nothing was ever attempted.

Also: LESSONS L-013, a CLAUDE.md hard rule, and the qa/review/iterate skills
updated to read the COVERAGE line rather than the PASS count, and to treat
PDF_DRIFT as "nothing was compared" rather than as a render defect.

_new_commits.body:
v1.9.57 diagnosed that one stray U+0008 BACKSPACE made a Frontiers running
header unequal to its layout-channel twin, and fixed it inside `_key()` — F0's
comparison key. The character stayed in the emitted text, where a completely
unrelated rule landed on it one day later:
`_prior_paragraph_is_sentence_terminated` walks back over whitespace and
requires what it finds to be in ".!?/". On 10.3389/fvets.2025.1645266 the walk
landed on the BACKSPACE, discarded the `1 Introduction:` heading, and greedy
span-fill handed the preceding KEYWORDS span 69,849 characters — the whole
article. Found by an external benchmark, not by us.

* C0 `_strip_furniture_controls` (NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.58), run before F0
  so the comparison key and the output are ONE rule. One character wide and
  measured: all 33 corpus U+0008 sites are '.'+BS+newline, none are overstrike.
  U+0002/03/04/07 are corrupted CONTENT glyphs (Schri<02>macher =
  "Schrittmacher") and are COUNTED, not stripped, in the new
  `NormalizationReport.residual_control_chars`.
* The heading guard skips page breaks and control characters, and a canonical
  heading carrying BOTH a line-initial section number AND a colon no longer
  needs a terminated prior paragraph (SECTIONING_VERSION 1.2.5). Both halves
  are required: `2 Literature search` on the same paper resolves canonically to
  `references`, so a number-only escape would open back-matter mid-article.
  Measured blast radius: 3 of 39 guard rejections were furniture; the escape
  fires exactly once in 30 papers.
* The boundary-truncation pass, unreachable since v1.6.1 (`_NO_TRUNCATE =
  set(SectionLabel)` matched every label), is deleted.

The C0 strip ALONE does not fix that paper — the first probe said it did,
because it stripped the character from an already-normalized string while the
shipped order runs C0 before H0. Test the composition that ships (LESSONS
L-055, L-056).

Arena effect, 30 held-out PMC papers: body-label slice 0.7681 -> 0.7911,
oracle 0.8038 -> 0.8140, collapses 5 -> 4, recall median 0.9862, 0 regressions.

render-deletion 26/26 with 0 content lost; verify_corpus 26/26 COVERAGE 26/26;

The entry said "16 papers gain page breaks; 2 footnote appendices restored" with
no indication of which callers see it. Two of those three claims do not reach the
HTTP API at all, and the entry as written told consumers otherwise.

`_f0_strip_running_and_footnotes` returns immediately without a `LayoutDoc`, and
the footnote appendix is F0's product. Enumerated rather than assumed:

    batch.py:355              passes layout   -> full change
    sections/__init__.py:116  passes layout   -> full change
    service/app/main.py:532   NO layout       -> page breaks only
    service/app/main.py:1007  NO layout       -> page breaks only

change (not 16), 0 appendices restored (not 2), and still 0 lines removed or

service never computes a layout, F0 has NEVER run in production, and neither has

_new_commits.message: test(gate): the docs-accuracy gate had no test, and was edited twice in one session
_new_commits.body:
`scripts/check_docs_consistency.py` asserts that the version numbers
`docs/README.md` advertises still match the constants this package defines. It is
invoked by hand from handoffs and release checklists and by nothing automatic —
so it was changed twice today (2657047, ab291c7) with nothing pinning either
change, and the second of those changes existed only because the first had a gap
nobody could have caught.

A check that CAN be a test MUST be a test. A gate nobody runs is
indistinguishable from a gate that passes, and this one guards a claim that
reaches consumers: `docs/README.md` documents the provenance block
`get_version_info()` returns.

Five cases, each pinning a failure that actually happened or is about to:

  * the gate PASSES on the committed tree
  * a drifted PACKAGE version is caught — the one that goes stale on EVERY
    release, uncovered until ab291c7
  * a drifted PIPELINE version is caught — `table_extraction_version` sat at
    '2.4.10' against a source 2.4.12 until it was spotted by eye
  * a drifted NORMALIZATION version is caught
  * the two deliberately-ungated keys are still NAMED in the gate, so the reason
    for excluding them cannot be silently lost

Each drift runs against a COPY of only the files the gate reads, in tmp — the
test never mutates the working tree, and does not drag the corpus along.

MUTATION-VERIFIED IN TWO DIRECTIONS, because a test that has never failed against
the real defect proves nothing:

  removing the package-version line   -> exactly 1 test fails
  removing the whole sibling loop     -> 3 tests fail

_new_commits.message: fix(gate): the version check missed the ONE version that goes stale every release
_new_commits.body:
Hard rule 23 says a universal-quantifier claim is only as good as the enumeration
behind it. The previous commit's message claimed the gate "compares every
advertised pipeline version against its defining constant". Enumerating the
provenance block in docs/README.md rather than trusting that sentence:

    advertised   version, normalize_version, sectioning_version,
                 table_extraction_version, python_version, unicodedata_version
    covered      normalize_version, sectioning_version, table_extraction_version
    UNCOVERED    version, python_version, unicodedata_version

Six keys, not the five I had in mind -- `unicodedata_version` was not even on my
list. The claim was defensible for the three PIPELINE versions and silent about
the rest, which is exactly the shape rule 23 exists to catch.

`version` is now covered, and it is the important one: it is the package version,
so it goes stale on EVERY release, and docs/README.md advertises it as `2.4.135`.
The very next release would have made that doc wrong with nothing to say so.

`python_version` and `unicodedata_version` are deliberately NOT gated, and the
code says why: they are runtime facts this repo does not define, so there is no
constant for them to drift from. Recording the reason matters more than the
exclusion -- an unexplained gap reads as an oversight to the next maintainer.

Mutation-verified: setting __version__ = 2.4.136 fails with
"docs/README.md says version = '2.4.135' but docpluck/__init__.py defines
__version__ = '2.4.136'", and restoring it passes.

r_meta.description_text: Provide reproducible R chunks in R Markdown document that automatically check computational results for reproducibility. This is achieved by creating json files storing metadata about computational results. A comprehensive tutorial to the package is available as preprint by Brandmaier & Peikert (2024, <doi:10.31234/osf.io/3zjvf>).

highlights.message: release: v2.4.137 — a fix in the COMPARISON KEY is not a fix in the SHIPPED string
highlights.body:
v1.9.57 diagnosed that one stray U+0008 BACKSPACE made a Frontiers running
header unequal to its layout-channel twin, and fixed it inside `_key()` — F0's
comparison key. The character stayed in the emitted text, where a completely
unrelated rule landed on it one day later:
`_prior_paragraph_is_sentence_terminated` walks back over whitespace and
requires what it finds to be in ".!?/". On 10.3389/fvets.2025.1645266 the walk
landed on the BACKSPACE, discarded the `1 Introduction:` heading, and greedy
span-fill handed the preceding KEYWORDS span 69,849 characters — the whole
article. Found by an external benchmark, not by us.

* C0 `_strip_furniture_controls` (NORMALIZATION_VERSION 1.9.58), run before F0
  so the comparison key and the output are ONE rule. One character wide and
  measured: all 33 corpus U+0008 sites are '.'+BS+newline, none are overstrike.
  U+0002/03/04/07 are corrupted CONTENT glyphs (Schri<02>macher =
  "Schrittmacher") and are COUNTED, not stripped, in the new
  `NormalizationReport.residual_control_chars`.
* The heading guard skips page breaks and control characters, and a canonical
  heading carrying BOTH a line-initial section number AND a colon no longer
  needs a terminated prior paragraph (SECTIONING_VERSION 1.2.5). Both halves
  are required: `2 Literature search` on the same paper resolves canonically to
  `references`, so a number-only escape would open back-matter mid-article.
  Measured blast radius: 3 of 39 guard rejections were furniture; the escape
  fires exactly once in 30 papers.
* The boundary-truncation pass, unreachable since v1.6.1 (`_NO_TRUNCATE =
  set(SectionLabel)` matched every label), is deleted.

The C0 strip ALONE does not fix that paper — the first probe said it did,
because it stripped the character from an already-normalized string while the
shipped order runs C0 before H0. Test the composition that ships (LESSONS
L-055, L-056).

Arena effect, 30 held-out PMC papers: body-label slice 0.7681 -> 0.7911,
oracle 0.8038 -> 0.8140, collapses 5 -> 4, recall median 0.9862, 0 regressions.

Gates: 2,885 passed / 0 failed; non-statistic corpus scan CLEAN 60/60;
render-deletion 26/26 with 0 content lost; verify_corpus 26/26 COVERAGE 26/26;
service suite 183 passed; public-repo hygiene 11/11.

highlights.message: docs(changelog): v2.4.136's measurements were the LAYOUT path, presented as universal
highlights.body:
The entry said "16 papers gain page breaks; 2 footnote appendices restored" with
no indication of which callers see it. Two of those three claims do not reach the
HTTP API at all, and the entry as written told consumers otherwise.

`_f0_strip_running_and_footnotes` returns immediately without a `LayoutDoc`, and
the footnote appendix is F0's product. Enumerated rather than assumed:

    batch.py:355              passes layout   -> full change
    sections/__init__.py:116  passes layout   -> full change
    service/app/main.py:532   NO layout       -> page breaks only
    service/app/main.py:1007  NO layout       -> page breaks only

Re-measured through the no-layout path the service actually runs: 12 of 26 papers
change (not 16), 0 appendices restored (not 2), and still 0 lines removed or
added. The API gains page boundaries and loses nothing; it gains no appendix.

AND THE LARGER FINDING, pre-existing and not this release's doing: because the
service never computes a layout, F0 has NEVER run in production, and neither has
any layout-gated repair -- W0h (dropped minus via cid glyph), W0m (beta-as-b via
font), W0p (superscript via size+baseline). Every API consumer has been receiving
text with running headers intact and those three repairs absent, while the same
document through `extract_to_dir` is repaired. Two paths, one version, different
numbers.

This is the identical shape CLAUDE.md records for batch.py and marks FIXED in
v2.4.128 -- the service was never checked. NOT fixed here: wiring a layout into
the service roughly doubles per-document cost and changes output for every
consumer at once, which is a deliberate decision, not a doc fix. Tracked in the
handoff and in both consumer notices.

highlights.message: release: v2.4.136 — a page NUMBER is furniture, a page BOUNDARY is structure
highlights.body:
Bumps __version__ + pyproject to 2.4.136 and promotes the CHANGELOG entry.
NORMALIZATION_VERSION was already at 1.9.57 (cd89380), because the output
changed then and the version describing that output had to move with it.

WHAT SHIPS. `_normalize_text` stripped standalone page numbers with
`^\s*\d{1,3}\s*$` under MULTILINE, and the whitespace class matches THE FORM
FEED — so the rule could consume the page boundary beside the number it deleted.
Wrong since it was written, held latent by a running footer standing between the
two. Two baseline papers were ALREADY broken at HEAD: 10.1016/j.jesp.2021.104154
and 10.1016/j.joep.2020.102350 reported 15 and 18 footnotes through
report.footnote_texts while the returned string carried no appendix at all.

separates the footnote appendix now actually appears on those papers. A consumer
splitting on it gets a body WITHOUT the footnotes where it previously got a body
WITH them silently inlined. That is a correction, but it is a change.

Measured, 26-paper baseline vs a git worktree of the prior tree, separate
interpreters: 0 lines removed, 0 added; 16 papers gain page breaks (+1..+17);
2 appendices restored (0 -> 1,288 and 0 -> 2,165 bytes); 0 papers worse.

docs/README.md's advertised `'version'` was updated — and it was the gate added
in ab291c7 that caught it going stale, on its first real release. That gate now

highlights.message: test(gate): the docs-accuracy gate had no test, and was edited twice in one session
highlights.body:
`scripts/check_docs_consistency.py` asserts that the version numbers
`docs/README.md` advertises still match the constants this package defines. It is
invoked by hand from handoffs and release checklists and by nothing automatic —
so it was changed twice today (2657047, ab291c7) with nothing pinning either
change, and the second of those changes existed only because the first had a gap
nobody could have caught.

A check that CAN be a test MUST be a test. A gate nobody runs is
indistinguishable from a gate that passes, and this one guards a claim that
reaches consumers: `docs/README.md` documents the provenance block
`get_version_info()` returns.

Five cases, each pinning a failure that actually happened or is about to:

  * the gate PASSES on the committed tree
  * a drifted PACKAGE version is caught — the one that goes stale on EVERY
    release, uncovered until ab291c7
  * a drifted PIPELINE version is caught — `table_extraction_version` sat at
    '2.4.10' against a source 2.4.12 until it was spotted by eye
  * a drifted NORMALIZATION version is caught
  * the two deliberately-ungated keys are still NAMED in the gate, so the reason
    for excluding them cannot be silently lost

Each drift runs against a COPY of only the files the gate reads, in tmp — the
test never mutates the working tree, and does not drag the corpus along.

MUTATION-VERIFIED IN TWO DIRECTIONS, because a test that has never failed against
the real defect proves nothing:

  removing the package-version line   -> exactly 1 test fails
  removing the whole sibling loop     -> 3 tests fail

highlights.message: fix(gate): the version check missed the ONE version that goes stale every release
highlights.body:
Hard rule 23 says a universal-quantifier claim is only as good as the enumeration
behind it. The previous commit's message claimed the gate "compares every
advertised pipeline version against its defining constant". Enumerating the
provenance block in docs/README.md rather than trusting that sentence:

    advertised   version, normalize_version, sectioning_version,
                 table_extraction_version, python_version, unicodedata_version
    covered      normalize_version, sectioning_version, table_extraction_version
    UNCOVERED    version, python_version, unicodedata_version

Six keys, not the five I had in mind -- `unicodedata_version` was not even on my
list. The claim was defensible for the three PIPELINE versions and silent about
the rest, which is exactly the shape rule 23 exists to catch.

`version` is now covered, and it is the important one: it is the package version,
so it goes stale on EVERY release, and docs/README.md advertises it as `2.4.135`.
The very next release would have made that doc wrong with nothing to say so.

`python_version` and `unicodedata_version` are deliberately NOT gated, and the
code says why: they are runtime facts this repo does not define, so there is no
constant for them to drift from. Recording the reason matters more than the
exclusion -- an unexplained gap reads as an oversight to the next maintainer.

Mutation-verified: setting __version__ = 2.4.136 fails with
"docs/README.md says version = '2.4.135' but docpluck/__init__.py defines
__version__ = '2.4.136'", and restoring it passes.

Now tracked from both osf_type()'s "inaccessible" classification and a later fetch failure (osf_get_all_pages()'s osf_error attribute), and named in both summary_text and the full report.

Tests use testthat::with_mocked_bindings() rather than local_mocked_bindings(): the latter's deferred cleanup does not restore correctly through this project's custom test_that() wrapper in helper.R and leaks into whichever test runs next (same class of issue test-archive-osf.R's .osf_status_error test already flags for req_perform()).

consume the page boundary standing beside the number it was deleting. It had been
wrong since it was written, and a running footer sitting between the two held it
latent. The moment anything stripped that footer, every form feed in the document
went with it -- and with them the `\n\f\f\n` marker that separates the footnote
appendix, folding it back into the body where a consumer reads it as running text.

Two papers in the render baseline were ALREADY in that state at HEAD: they report
15 and 18 footnotes through `report.footnote_texts` while the returned string
carries no appendix at all. Nothing had ever noticed, because nothing compared
the two.

MEASURED, 26-paper baseline vs a `git worktree` of HEAD, extracted in separate
interpreters and diffed per field:

    lines removed / added (full text)     0 / 0
    papers gaining page breaks           16   (+1 to +17 each)
    footnote appendices RESTORED          2   (0 -> 1,288 and 0 -> 2,165 bytes)
    papers made worse on any metric        0

The rule is now `_strip_standalone_page_numbers()` -- a named function, so its
test pins THE SHIPPED RULE rather than a retyped copy of the pattern. The form
feed is CAPTURED and put back, not merely excluded from the class: a page number
is often the first thing on a new page, so the line itself begins with the break,
and excluding it stopped those lines matching at all ('496'..'502' reappeared in
the body of 10.1016/j.jesp.2009.12.010). `_drop()` in F0's strip loop keeps the
same promise from the other side -- the segment split attaches a separator to the
line BEFORE it, so deleting a running footer deleted its page break too.

All three guards mutation-verified: the original defect fails two tests, the
`[ \t]` half-fix fails one, neutering `_drop()` fails one. That last became a
real test only after the fixture was corrected -- it first put the furniture at
the TOP of each page, so its separator was a newline, `_drop()` was never
reached, and the test passed with the guard removed.

`_key` is hoisted to module level and strips non-whitespace control characters
(pdftotext emits a running header as FF + text + BACKSPACE). It is a correctness
fix to a key BOTH channels use; it changes no measured output today and its test
says so plainly rather than implying a capability.

ALSO: tools/diag/fused_cell_geometry_scan.py, the FUSED-GRID detector register
G6h was blocked on until v2.4.135 gave every Camelot cell a verified rectangle.
Validated on the census's own known positives before any count was quoted --
'104594' fires at 15.15 em (136.4 pt) between '4' and '5', '4.603.804.80' at
12.22 em. 80 fused cells, 1.13% of 7,065 measured, against the text-only
census's 34 (0.29%). Threshold measured, not chosen: 71,733 intra-cell gaps give
p50=0.00 p90=0.00 p99=0.33 em, so 0.75 sits in an empty band. It REFUSES any cell
whose recovered glyphs are not its own text (3,139 of 10,215) rather than folding
them into the denominator -- the first draft did not, and reported 17.3 em
"fusions" that were column gutters between two cells.

TWO REVERTS, both recorded because the reasoning is worth more than the code:

W0g/W0b/W0d are untouched here, but W0g is now DECIDED for deletion in its own
release: re-measured at 12 sites in 4 of 250 papers where the record said 4, and

the rasterized page -- 10.1525/collabra.118835 p7 prints
`hedges' g = -.17, SE = 0.11, ...` and W0g emits `SE = -0.11`.

highlights.message: feat(tables): real per-cell geometry, behind a round-trip identity guard (register A1/G6a)
highlights.body:
Every Camelot cell shipped `(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)` while Camelot itself held the
real coordinates for each one. Reading `ct.cells[r][c]` is one line; it took two
releases because EVERY way of getting it wrong produces WRONG coordinates rather
than empty ones, and a wrong bbox is worse than none - it answers, plausibly, and
the answer is off by a page. Register G4 deferred the work until the guard could
be built first. Building the guard found TWO MORE TRAPS G4 never listed, both
live on real papers:

  T5  Camelot silently ROTATES a page whose text is sideways and reports
      coordinates in that frame. 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.39337 p8:
      rotation=anticlockwise, pdf_size=(792,612), table bbox reaching x=730.7 -
      off-page in pdfplumber's 612-wide frame - while pdfplumber reports
      rotation=0. Also 10.1017/s0007123424000024 p6 (clockwise), whose converted
      boxes come out with a NEGATIVE top. 2 of 8 papers probed.
  T6  `_augment_lattice_with_stream_rows` pd.concat's stream rows onto `ct.df`
      and never touches `ct.cells`. 10.1038/s41598-023-50423-7 ships df=61x4
      against cells=20x4; zipping by index would give 41 rows of published data
      another row's rectangle.

THE GUARD. Each rectangle is converted to pdfplumber space, `chars_in_bbox` is
asked what stands there, and the result scored by character-multiset CONTAINMENT.
Exact equality is the wrong predicate and the probe said so before the code was
written: Camelot assigns a whole text object to ONE grid cell even when its
glyphs spill past that cell's column edges. Measured - per cell 86.3% score >=
0.95 under the correct transform against 2.1%/1.5%/1.5% under T1/T2/T3; per TABLE
the median correct score is 0.98 while ALL 200 tables fall below 0.30 under every
trap. Gate 0.60, in a real gap: the lowest ACCEPTED table scores 0.70, the two
rejected 0.55 and 0.53. All-or-nothing per table.

Verification is SAMPLED (40 cells, fixed stride - never random); the geometry is
not. `chars_in_bbox` is O(chars-on-page), so full verification costs 78.9
ms/table and grows with the grid, on the service's per-request path; the cap
makes it 40.0 ms/table independent of size and changed NO verdict across 200
tables.

The three row-trims each gained an index-returning `_keep_after_*` sibling and
became one-liners over it - one implementation, two views, so the raw-row mapping
cannot drift from the trim. Behaviour verified identical to the originals over
6,002 generated matrices.

`Table["cell_geometry"]` is new, on EVERY table from EVERY path: "verified:<f>"
or the named refusal. An earlier draft set it only on the Camelot path and the
census caught 11.6% of tables reporting nothing - which both hid the state and
UNDERSTATED what we ship, since the whitespace path's boxes are built from
pdfplumber words and are real by construction.

* census (tools/diag/cell_geometry_census.py, 12 papers, 69 tables): 81.2%
  verified, 10.1% no_cells, 2.9% roundtrip_failed, 2.9% grid_shape_mismatch,

* content-neutrality: every corpus paper extracted under BOTH v2.4.134 (git
  worktree) and this tree, separate interpreters - 72 tables, 72 identical, 0
  differing;
* full suite: 2840 passed, 27 skipped, 5 xfailed, 0 failed (1:03:51). 2872
  collected = the previous 2862 plus this release's 10 geometry tests.

THIS IS THE FOUNDATION, NOT THE FIX. Register J's two open text-loss defects and
the FUSED-GRID class (G6h) are unblocked, not closed.

highlights.message: fix(cleanup): the temp-PDF guard covered TWO of the library's FIVE sites, and said "BOTH"
highlights.body:
v2.4.134 fixed a temp-PDF leak in camelot_extract.py and wrote, beside the fix,
"BOTH call sites, because a fix applied to one of two is not fixed, and this
module has a documented history of exactly that". True of the module, false of
the library: `grep -rn 'NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".pdf", delete=False)'
docpluck/` returns FIVE sites.

    extract.py:249            bare os.unlink, NO guard  -> raises out of extract_pdf
    extract_columns.py:292    except Exception: pass    -> silent
    extract_columns.py:965    except Exception: pass    -> silent
    tables/camelot_extract.py:834  _unlink_temp_pdf     -> retried + recorded
    tables/camelot_extract.py:947  _unlink_temp_pdf     -> retried + recorded

REPRODUCED, not reasoned about. Forcing the unlink to raise PermissionError
[WinError 32] - the error already documented on this machine at the sibling site
- makes extract_pdf, extract_pdf_structured and render_pdf_to_markdown propagate
it AFTER the text has already been extracted successfully, with no record
anywhere. Inside extract_structured that reaches a broad `except`, reads as
"camelot failed", and zeroes every table on a document whose extraction entirely
succeeded (incident 2026-06-13). Red-first: 4 failed / 8 passed before, 13 after.

Nothing was leaking - instrumented per entry point, all five delete their temp
file every time. The defect is what happens when one cannot.

The invariant is now stated once and held everywhere: a temp-PDF cleanup failure
must never propagate out of an extraction entry point, and must never be silent.
docpluck/tempfiles.py::unlink_temp_pdf is the one implementation; all five sites
call it; camelot_extract._unlink_temp_pdf remains a deprecated alias. Telemetry
key renamed camelot_temp_pdf_not_deleted -> temp_pdf_not_deleted (absent from
v2.4.126, so unreleased and free to rename).

ALSO: the gate that was guarding this could not see its own property.
test_camelot_temp_pdf_is_not_leaked asserted `after <= before` over a glob of the
machine's SHARED temp directory. Measured both ways: run alone it goes RED (+1)
while docpluck's telemetry reports zero cleanup failures - another process's temp
file alive at the instant of the count, which need not leak, only be
mid-extraction; run WITH a concurrent extractor it goes GREEN. Replaced by
tests/test_temp_pdf_cleanup_invariant.py, which spies on
tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile and checks the paths THIS process created.

This commit also carries CHANGELOG.md, LESSONS.md (L-050) and
docs/OVERHAUL_REGISTER.md (J15) for the whole v2.4.134 release, since those files
hold content from every session in it and cannot be split by file.

highlights.body:
The body of the release, authored across the sessions preceding 2026-08-19 and
uncommitted until now. Full account in CHANGELOG.md [2.4.134] and
docs/OVERHAUL_REGISTER.md sections F-J; the highlights:

* separation of duties executed - A2, A3a and W0n DELETED because they repaired
  the PAPER rather than canonicalising NOTATION, each retired on a measurement
  rather than a judgement;
* the EU->US numeric conversion rules and the document-level locale inference
  removed entirely: over 297 English papers they fired 10 times in 3 papers and
  not once correctly, and the detector was confidently wrong on the only genuine
  European table ever found;
* W0h/W0m pair their evidence by IDENTITY rather than position, so a glyph proven
  on page 7 can no longer license flipping a token on page 2 (reproduced with a
  planted decoy: the old code flipped the decoy AND left the real coefficient
  corrupt);
* the render channel stopped deleting published statistics, and gained telemetry
  for the first time - it had been chaining 54 `md = fn(md)` calls and returning
  a bare str;
* Camelot confidence is Camelot's own formula applied to the grid we ship, with
  its components exposed;
* DOCX OMML equations survive instead of being silently dropped - measured 15% of
  papers, and every affected span was an effect size;
* one Greek table (docpluck/symbols.py) instead of two that disagreed on 9 of 9
  shared letters.

Docs, LESSONS and the register describing this work land in the two commits that
follow, because they also carry the 2026-08-19 sessions' changes and cannot be
split by file.
